Berbers.fact: Sanchuelo was left with only a few followers, and was captured and killed in 1009.

Berbers.fact: Hisham II abdicated and was succeeded by Muhammad II al-Mahdi. Marching on Cordoba, they defeated Saqaliba general Wadih and forced Muhammad II al-Mahdi to flee to Toledo.

Berbers.fact: They obtained logistical support from Count Sancho Garcia of Castile.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Marching on _____, they defeated Saqaliba general Wadih and forced Muhammad II al-Mahdi to flee to Toledo
Berbers.fact: Marching on Cordoba, they defeated Saqaliba general Wadih and forced Muhammad II al-Mahdi to flee to Toledo. Wadih and al-Mahdi formed an alliance with the Counts of Barcelona and Urgell and marched back on Cordoba.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They then installed _____ as caliph, and based themselves in the Madinat al-Zahra to avoid friction with the local population
Berbers.fact: Having abandoned Sanchuelo, the Berbers who had formed his army turned to support another ambitious Umayyad, Sulayman. They then installed Sulayman as caliph, and based themselves in the Madinat al-Zahra to avoid friction with the local population.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Wadih and al-Mahdi formed an alliance with the Counts of _____ and Urgell and marched back on Cordoba
Berbers.fact: Wadih and al-Mahdi formed an alliance with the Counts of Barcelona and Urgell and marched back on Cordoba.

Berbers.fact: They defeated Sulayman and the Berber forces in a battle near Cordoba in 1010.

Berbers.fact: However, he was defeated in battle near Marbella.

Berbers.fact: The Berbers turned around and besieged Cordoba. They methodically destroyed Cordoba's suburbs, pinning the inhabitants inside the old Roman walls and destroying the Madinat al-Zahra.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: They methodically destroyed Cordoba's suburbs, pinning the inhabitants inside the old Roman walls and destroying the Madinat al-Zahra. Wadih's allies killed him, and the Cordoba garrison surrendered with the expectation of amnesty.

Berbers.fact: Ibn Idhari said that the installation of Sulayman in 1013 was the moment when "the rule of the Berbers began in Cordoba and that of the Umayyads ended, after it had existed for two hundred and sixty eight years and forty-three days". Berbers.fact: Ibn Idhari said that the installation of Sulayman in 1013 was the moment when "the rule of the Berbers began in Cordoba and that of the Umayyads ended, after it had existed for two hundred and sixty eight years and forty-three days". After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms.

Berbers.fact: The Taifa period ended when a Berber dynasty—the Moroccan Almoravids—took over al-Andalus; they were succeeded by the Almohad dynasty of Morocco, during which time al-Andalus flourished.

Berbers.fact: After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms. One group of Saqaliba seized Orihuela from its Berber garrison and took control of the entire region.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: After the fall of Cordoba, the Zirids took over Granada in _____, forming the Zirid kingdom of Granada
Berbers.fact: After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms. After the fall of Cordoba, the Zirids took over Granada in 1013, forming the Zirid kingdom of Granada.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in 1018, but failed.

Berbers.fact: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in 1018, but failed. Khayran then executed Abd ar-Rahman IV.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Khayran's son, Zuhayr, also made war on the Zirid kingdom of Granada, but was killed in _____
Berbers.fact: Khayran's son, Zuhayr, also made war on the Zirid kingdom of Granada, but was killed in 1038.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: After being installed as caliph with Berber support, Sulayman was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies.

Berbers.fact: The Zenata Berber Hammudids received the important districts of Ceuta and Algeciras.

Berbers.fact: In 1016 they rebelled in Ceuta, claiming to be supporting the restoration of Hisham II.

Berbers.fact: The last Hammudid caliph reigned until 1027.

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids remained in Málaga until expelled by the Zirids in 1056.

Berbers.fact: The Zirids of Granada controlled Málaga until 1073, after which separate Zirid kings retained control over the taifas of Granada and Malaga until the Almoravid conquest.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: During the taifa period, the Aftasid dynasty, based in Badajoz, controlled a large territory centered on the Guadiana River valley. Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: According to Bernard Reilly, during the taifa period genealogy continued to be an obsession of the upper classes in al-Andalus.

Berbers.fact: Most wanted to trace their lineage back to the Syrian and Yemeni Arabs who accompanied the invasion.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Malikite disciple Abd Allah ibn Yasin accepted the invitation.

Berbers.fact: Traveling to Morocco, he set up a military monastery or ribat where he trained a highly motivated and disciplined fighting force.

Berbers.fact: In 1054 and 1055, employing these specially trained forces, Almoravid leader Yahya ibn Umar defeated the Kingdom of Ghana and the Zenata Berber.

Berbers.fact: Forced to resolve a Sanhaja civil war, he left control of the Moroccan conquests to his brother, Yusuf ibn Tashfin.

Berbers.fact: After the fall of Toledo to Alfonso VI in 1085, al-Mutamid appealed again to Yusuf.

Berbers.fact: Tamazight is now taught in Aurès since the march led by Salim Yezza in 2004.

Berbers.fact: E1b1b1b accounts for 45% of North Africans, while Haplogroup J1-M267 accounts for 30% of North Africans, and has spread from Arabia.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: They also became involved in debates over the relationship between the CNT and the Spanish anarchist movement.

Cao Fang.fact: Many of Cao's associates, such as Deng Yang (鄧颺), Li Sheng (李勝), He Yan (何晏), and Ding Mi (丁謐), were appointed as high-ranking officials.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Sima was granted military authority, including command in defending _____ from Eastern Wu's attack in 241, but he had no real authority on governance
Cao Fang.fact: Sima was granted military authority, including command in defending Cao Wei from Eastern Wu's attack in 241, but he had no real authority on governance.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: In 244, _____ led an attack on Shu Han's border city of Hanzhong, without careful planning, hoping that he would gain a reputation in the military
Cao Fang.fact: In 244, Cao Shuang led an attack on Shu Han's border city of Hanzhong, without careful planning, hoping that he would gain a reputation in the military.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: The battles were inconclusive and Cao was forced to withdraw with great losses when their food supplies ran out (Battle of _____)
Cao Fang.fact: The battles were inconclusive and Cao was forced to withdraw with great losses when their food supplies ran out (Battle of Xingshi).

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: In 247, _____ retired from government service, claiming that he was ill
Cao Fang.fact: In 247, Sima Yi retired from government service, claiming that he was ill.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Cao Shuang eventually decided to surrender his authority, against the advice of _____
Cao Fang.fact: Cao Shuang eventually decided to surrender his authority, against the advice of Huan Fan.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Sima promised _____ that he could still retain his titles
Cao Fang.fact: While Cao Fang and Cao Shuang left the capital Luoyang to visit Cao Rui's tomb, Sima rallied a group of anti-Cao Shuang officials and closed all gates of Luoyang. He sent an edict to Cao Fang in the name of Empress Dowager Guo, accusing Cao Shuang of dominating and corrupting the government, and demanding that Cao Shuang and his brothers be removed from power.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: However, a few days later, Sima had _____ and his family and associates executed on charges of treason
Cao Fang.fact: He sent an edict to Cao Fang in the name of Empress Dowager Guo, accusing Cao Shuang of dominating and corrupting the government, and demanding that Cao Shuang and his brothers be removed from power. Cao Shuang eventually decided to surrender his authority, against the advice of Huan Fan.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: By then, _____ was in complete control of the government
Cao Fang.fact: By then, Sima Yi was in complete control of the government. In 249, Wang Ling, the general in charge of the southeastern city of Shouchun, plotted a rebellion against Sima Yi, in association with Cao Biao (曹彪), the Prince of Chu.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: In 249, _____, the general in charge of the southeastern city of Shouchun, plotted a rebellion against Sima Yi, in association with Cao Biao (曹彪), the Prince of Chu
Cao Fang.fact: In 249, Wang Ling, the general in charge of the southeastern city of Shouchun, plotted a rebellion against Sima Yi, in association with Cao Biao (曹彪), the Prince of Chu.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: In 251, when Wang was ready to carry out his plan, his subordinates _____ (黃華) and Yang Hong (楊弘) betrayed him to Sima
Cao Fang.fact: In 251, when Wang was ready to carry out his plan, his subordinates Huang Hua (黃華) and Yang Hong (楊弘) betrayed him to Sima.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Sima led an army to _____ before Wang could take action, and promised to pardon Wang for rebelling
Cao Fang.fact: In 249, Wang Ling, the general in charge of the southeastern city of Shouchun, plotted a rebellion against Sima Yi, in association with Cao Biao (曹彪), the Prince of Chu. Sima led an army to Shouchun before Wang could take action, and promised to pardon Wang for rebelling.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Wang surrendered and was forced to commit suicide together with _____ later
Cao Fang.fact: In 249, Wang Ling, the general in charge of the southeastern city of Shouchun, plotted a rebellion against Sima Yi, in association with Cao Biao (曹彪), the Prince of Chu. Wang surrendered and was forced to commit suicide together with Cao Biao later.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Sima Yi died later in _____ that year and was succeeded by his son Sima Shi as regent, who continued wielding state power
Cao Fang.fact: Sima Yi died later in September that year and was succeeded by his son Sima Shi as regent, who continued wielding state power.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: In 253, Sima defeated _____ in a major battle and established a reputation in the military
Cao Fang.fact: In 253, Sima defeated Zhuge Ke in a major battle and set up a reputation in the military.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Sima beat Li to death with a sword handle and accused Li and his associates _____ and Zhang Ji (張緝) of treason, and had them and their clans exterminated
Cao Fang.fact: Sima beat Li to death with a sword handle and accused Li and his associates Xiahou Xuan and Zhang Ji (張緝) of treason, and had them and their clans exterminated.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Cao Fang () (_____–274), courtesy name Lanqing, was the third and longest-reigning emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period
Cao Fang.fact: Cao Fang () (232–274), courtesy name Lanqing, was the third and longest-reigning emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: Cao's life was spared and he was demoted to his previous title of _____ of Qi
Cao Fang.fact: Cao's life was spared and he was demoted to his previous title of Prince of Qi. When Sima Zhao's son Sima Yan usurped the throne of Cao Wei in February 266 and set up the Jin dynasty, Cao Fang and other Cao Wei princes were demoted to the status of dukes.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: He died in 274 and was posthumously granted the title of "_____ of Shaoling", with a funeral befitting that of a duke instead of an emperor
Cao Fang.fact: He died in 274 and was posthumously granted the title of "Duke Li of Shaoling", with a funeral befitting that of a duke instead of an emperor.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: "young emperor of Wei") _____ of Wei (魏廢帝; lit
Cao Fang.fact: "young emperor of Wei") Emperor Fei of Wei (魏廢帝; lit.

Cao Fang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Fang.question: 251) _____, of the Zhang clan (張皇后) Empress, of the Wang clan (王皇后)
Cao Fang.fact: 251) Empress, of the Zhang clan (張皇后) Empress, of the Wang clan (王皇后).

Cao Guojiu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Guojiu.question: The _____ was One of the Eight Taoist Immortals.
Cao Guojiu.fact: Cao Guojiu, literally Imperial Brother-in-law Cao, is a Chinese mythological figure and one of the Eight Immortals in the Taoist pantheon.

Cao Guojiu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Guojiu.question: His real name was _____ while his courtesy name was Jingxiu, and he was better known to his contemporaries as Cao Jingxiu
Cao Guojiu.fact: His real name was Cao Yi while his courtesy name was Jingxiu, and he was better known to his contemporaries as Cao Jingxiu.

Cao Guojiu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Guojiu.question: Cao's younger brother, _____ (曹景植), abused his relationship with the imperial family by bullying others and engaging in corrupt practices
Cao Guojiu.fact: Cao's younger brother, Cao Jingzhi (曹景植), abused his relationship with the imperial family by bullying others and engaging in corrupt practices. One day, Cao Jingzhi was accused by other officials in the imperial court of corruption and abuse of power.

Cao Guojiu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Guojiu.question: One day, _____ was accused by other officials in the imperial court of corruption and abuse of power
Cao Guojiu.fact: Cao's younger brother, Cao Jingzhi (曹景植), abused his relationship with the imperial family by bullying others and engaging in corrupt practices. One day, Cao Jingzhi was accused by other officials in the imperial court of corruption and abuse of power.

Cao Guojiu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Guojiu.question: During this time, he met the immortals _____ and Lü Dongbin, who taught him Taoist magical arts
Cao Guojiu.fact: During this time, he met the immortals Zhongli Quan and Lü Dongbin, who taught him Taoist magical arts.

Cao Guojiu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Guojiu.question: In other versions of his myth, he was _____'s actual brother and attempted to reform Renzong due to his political corruption
Cao Guojiu.fact: In other versions of his myth, he was Emperor Renzong's actual brother and attempted to reform Renzong due to his political corruption.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: The _____ was Chinese military general (died 232).
Cao Hong.fact: Cao Hong (died 232), courtesy name Zilian, was a Chinese military general of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China. Because of this connection, Cao Hong gained an official appointment as the Chief (長) of Qichun County (蘄春縣; northwest of present-day Qichun County, Hubei).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: He started his career in the late _____ dynasty under the warlord Cao Cao, who was his older second cousin
Cao Hong.fact: He started his career in the late Eastern Han dynasty under the warlord Cao Cao, who was his older second cousin.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Cao Cao engaged _____'s general Xu Rong at the Battle of Xingyang, but was defeated and forced to retreat
Cao Hong.fact: Around 190, the warlord Cao Cao, an older second cousin of Cao Hong, raised an army to participate in the campaign against the tyrannical warlord Dong Zhuo, who controlled the Han central government. Cao Cao engaged Dong Zhuo's general Xu Rong at the Battle of Xingyang, but was defeated and forced to retreat.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: They crossed the river and returned to Cao Cao's hometown in _____ (譙縣; present-day Bozhou, Anhui) safely
Cao Hong.fact: They crossed the river and returned to Cao Cao's hometown in Qiao County (譙縣; present-day Bozhou, Anhui) safely.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: He asked for troops from _____, who provided him with 2,000 of his best soldiers
Cao Hong.fact: Chen Wen (陳溫), the Inspector of Yang Province, was on friendly terms with Cao Hong. He asked for troops from Chen Wen, who provided him with 2,000 of his best soldiers.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: He brought along his 4,000 troops to meet Cao Cao at Longkang (龍亢; in present-day _____, Anhui) and became one of Cao Cao's most loyal followers since then
Cao Hong.fact: He brought along his 4,000 troops to meet Cao Cao at Longkang (龍亢; in present-day Huaiyuan County, Anhui) and became one of Cao Cao's most loyal followers since then.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Around the time, a famine had broken out in _____
Cao Hong.fact: Around the time, a famine had broken out in Yan Province.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: After that, Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu at _____ (濮陽縣; west of present-day Puyang County, Henan) and defeated him
Cao Hong.fact: After that, Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu at Puyang County (濮陽縣; west of present-day Puyang County, Henan) and defeated him.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Cao Cao subsequently attacked and retook Dong'e (東阿), Jiyin (濟陰), _____ (山陽), Zhongmu (中牟), Yangwu (陽武), Jing (京), Mi (密) and other counties from Lü Bu
Cao Hong.fact: Cao Cao subsequently attacked and retook Dong'e (東阿), Jiyin (濟陰), Shanyang (山陽), Zhongmu (中牟), Yangwu (陽武), Jing (京), Mi (密) and other counties from Lü Bu.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: In August 196, Cao Cao led his forces into Luoyang and received _____
Cao Hong.fact: In August 196, Cao Cao led his forces into Luoyang and received Emperor Xian.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Two months later, he relocated the emperor to his own base in Xu (許; present-day _____, Henan), where the new imperial capital was established
Cao Hong.fact: Two months later, he relocated the emperor to his own base in Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan), where the new imperial capital was set up. After Cao Cao left Wuyin County and returned to Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan), the officials in Nanyang (南陽), Zhangling (章陵) and other counties who had surrendered to him earlier rebelled and defected to Zhang Xiu's side.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: The garrison came under multiple attacks by _____ and his ally Liu Biao
Cao Hong.fact: After Cao Cao left Wuyin County and returned to Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan), the officials in Nanyang (南陽), Zhangling (章陵) and other counties who had surrendered to him earlier rebelled and defected to Zhang Xiu's side. The garrison came under multiple attacks by Zhang Xiu and his ally Liu Biao.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Cao Cao succeeded in destroying _____'s supplies in the raid and killed Chunyu Qiong in battle
Cao Hong.fact: When both sides were locked in a stalemate around winter, Cao Cao heeded the advice of Xu You, a defector from Yuan Shao's side, and personally led 5,000 riders to raid Yuan's supply depot at Wuchao (烏巢; southeast of present-day Yanjin County, Henan), which was guarded by Chunyu Qiong. Cao Cao succeeded in destroying Yuan Shao's supplies in the raid and killed Chunyu Qiong in battle.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: When Yuan Shao heard that _____ was under attack, he sent his generals Zhang He and Gao Lan (高覽) to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao's attention away from Wuchao
Cao Hong.fact: When both sides were locked in a stalemate around winter, Cao Cao heeded the advice of Xu You, a defector from Yuan Shao's side, and personally led 5,000 riders to raid Yuan's supply depot at Wuchao (烏巢; southeast of present-day Yanjin County, Henan), which was guarded by Chunyu Qiong. When Yuan Shao heard that Wuchao was under attack, he sent his generals Zhang He and Gao Lan (高覽) to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao's attention away from Wuchao.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: However, _____ and Gao Lan, already frustrated with Yuan Shao, ended up defecting to Cao Cao's side instead
Cao Hong.fact: When Yuan Shao heard that Wuchao was under attack, he sent his generals Zhang He and Gao Lan (高覽) to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao's attention away from Wuchao. However, Zhang He and Gao Lan, already frustrated with Yuan Shao, ended up defecting to Cao Cao's side instead.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: For his achievements, he was promoted to General of _____ (厲鋒將軍) and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Guoming Village (國明亭侯)
Cao Hong.fact: For his achievements, he was promoted to General of Sharp Edge (厲鋒將軍) and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Guoming Village (國明亭侯).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Later, as he made more contributions in battles, he was further promoted to _____-General (都護將軍)
Cao Hong.fact: Later, as he made more contributions in battles, he was further promoted to Protector-General (都護將軍).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Wu Lan was slain by _____ (強端), a Di chieftain from Yinping (陰平)
Cao Hong.fact: Wu Lan was slain by Qiangduan (強端), a Di chieftain from Yinping (陰平).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Later that year, his son and successor _____ ended the Eastern Han dynasty and established the state of Cao Wei with himself as the emperor
Cao Hong.fact: Later that year, his son and successor Cao Pi ended the Eastern Han dynasty and set up the state of Cao Wei with himself as the emperor. Cao Pi appointed Cao Hong as General of the Guards (衞將軍) and promoted him to General of Agile Cavalry (驃騎將軍).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: When Cao Cao was still the _____ of Works, he set an example by getting the county offices to keep records of the accounts of officials, including his
Cao Hong.fact: When Cao Cao was still the Minister of Works, he set an example by getting the county offices to keep records of the accounts of officials, including his. When his ministers tried to persuade him to spare Cao Hong, Cao Pi refused to listen.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Around _____, the warlord Cao Cao, an older second cousin of Cao Hong, raised an army to participate in the campaign against the tyrannical warlord Dong Zhuo, who controlled the Han central government
Cao Hong.fact: Around 190, the warlord Cao Cao, an older second cousin of Cao Hong, raised an army to participate in the campaign against the tyrannical warlord Dong Zhuo, who controlled the Han central government.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: In 224, when _____ returned from a campaign, Cao Pi ordered Wu Zhi to host a banquet in his residence in Cao Zhen's honour
Cao Hong.fact: Apparently, Cao Hong had previously offended Cao Zhen, another relative of Cao Cao who also served as a general in Wei. In 224, when Cao Zhen returned from a campaign, Cao Pi ordered Wu Zhi to host a banquet in his residence in Cao Zhen's honour.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: During the banquet, Wu Zhi instructed actors to put up a skit to make fun of _____ and Zhu Shuo (朱鑠), who were fat and thin respectively
Cao Hong.fact: Apparently, Cao Hong had previously offended Cao Zhen, another relative of Cao Cao who also served as a general in Wei. In 224, when Cao Zhen returned from a campaign, Cao Pi ordered Wu Zhi to host a banquet in his residence in Cao Zhen's honour.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Cao Pi died in June 226 and was succeeded by his son, _____, as the emperor of Wei
Cao Hong.fact: Cao Pi died in June 226 and was succeeded by his son, Cao Rui, as the emperor of Wei. Cao Rui rehabilitated Cao Hong by appointing him as General of the Rear (後將軍) and enfeoffing him as the Marquis of Lecheng (樂城侯) with 1,000 taxable households as his marquisate.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: His title, _____ of Lecheng (樂城侯), was passed on to his son, Cao Fu (曹馥)
Cao Hong.fact: Cao Rui rehabilitated Cao Hong by appointing him as General of the Rear (後將軍) and enfeoffing him as the Marquis of Lecheng (樂城侯) with 1,000 taxable households as his marquisate. Cao Hong died in 232 and was given the posthumous title "Marquis Gong" (恭侯), which means "humble(d) marquis".

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: She died a few years after their marriage, and _____ was so grieved by her death that he also died a few years later
Cao Hong.fact: Cao Hong's daughter, who was known for her beautiful looks, married Xun Can, a son of Xun Yu. She died a few years after their marriage, and Xun Can was so grieved by her death that he also died a few years later.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: The _____ was Emperor of Cao Wei from 260 to 266.
Cao Huan.fact: Cao Huan () (246 – 302/303), courtesy name Jingming, was the fifth and last emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period. After his abdication, Cao Huan was granted the title "Prince of Chenliu" and held it until his death, after which he was posthumously honoured as "Emperor Yuan (of Cao Wei)".

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: On 4 _____ 266, he abdicated the throne in favour of regent Sima Yan (later Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty), and brought an end to the Wei regime
Cao Huan.fact: On 4 February 266, he abdicated the throne in favour of regent Sima Yan (later Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty), and brought an end to the Wei regime.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: His father, _____, the Prince of Yan, was a son of Cao Cao, the father of Wei's first emperor, Cao Pi
Cao Huan.fact: His father, Cao Yu, the Prince of Yan, was a son of Cao Cao, the father of Wei's first emperor, Cao Pi.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: In late 263, _____, then Shu emperor, surrendered to Deng, bringing an end to the state of Shu
Cao Huan.fact: In late 263, Liu Shan, then Shu emperor, surrendered to Deng, bringing an end to the state of Shu.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: After the fall of Shu, _____ was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command
Cao Huan.fact: While Jiang Wei's attacks were largely easily repelled, Sima Zhao eventually ordered a counterattack on Shu with an invading force of 180,000 men commanded by Zhong Hui and Deng Ai. After the fall of Shu, Deng Ai was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: In early 264, _____ plotted with Jiang Wei to restore Shu and eliminate all the Wei generals who might oppose him
Cao Huan.fact: While Jiang Wei's attacks were largely easily repelled, Sima Zhao eventually ordered a counterattack on Shu with an invading force of 180,000 men commanded by Zhong Hui and Deng Ai. After the fall of Shu, Deng Ai was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: However, the generals started a counterinsurgency and killed _____ and Jiang Wei
Cao Huan.fact: After the fall of Shu, Deng Ai was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command. In early 264, Zhong Hui plotted with Jiang Wei to restore Shu and eliminate all the Wei generals who might oppose him.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: Shu's former territories (in present-day _____, Chongqing, Yunnan, southern Shaanxi, and southeastern Gansu) were completely annexed by Wei
Cao Huan.fact: Shu's former territories (in present-day Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, southern Shaanxi, and southeastern Gansu) were completely annexed by Wei.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: In May 264, _____ became a vassal king under the title "King of Jin" — the final step before usurpation
Cao Huan.fact: In December 263, Sima Zhao again forced Cao Huan to grant him the nine bestowments and this time he finally accepted, signifying that a usurpation was near; at the same time he was also made Duke of Jin. In May 264, Sima Zhao became a vassal king under the title "King of Jin" — the final step before usurpation.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: Sima Yan then established the Jin dynasty on 8 _____
Cao Huan.fact: After Sima Zhao died in September 265, his son, Sima Yan, inherited his father's position and on 4 February 266 forced Cao Huan to abdicate. Sima Yan then set up the Jin dynasty on 8 February.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: Sima Yan (posthumously known as _____ of Jin) permitted him to retain imperial banners and wagons and to worship ancestors with imperial ceremonies
Cao Huan.fact: Sima Yan (posthumously called Emperor Wu of Jin) permitted him to retain imperial banners and wagons and to worship ancestors with imperial ceremonies. He died in 302 during the reign of Emperor Wu's son, Emperor Hui.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: He died in 302 during the reign of _____'s son, Emperor Hui
Cao Huan.fact: Sima Yan (posthumously called Emperor Wu of Jin) permitted him to retain imperial banners and wagons and to worship ancestors with imperial ceremonies. He died in 302 during the reign of Emperor Wu's son, Emperor Hui.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: He was buried with honours due an emperor and given the posthumous name "_____" by the Jin court
Cao Huan.fact: He was buried with honours due an emperor and given the posthumous name "Yuan" by the Jin court.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: He was succeeded by his son, _____, whose title was confirmed on 24 November 363
Cao Huan.fact: He was succeeded by his son, Cao Hui, whose title was confirmed on 24 November 363.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: The _____ was Chinese general and warlord (1862–1938).
Cao Kun.fact: General Cao Kun (simplified Chinese: 曹锟; traditional Chinese: 曹錕; pinyin: Cáo Kūn; Wade–Giles: Ts'ao K'un; courtesy name: Zhongshan (仲珊); December 12, 1862 – May 15, 1938) was a Chinese warlord and politician, who served as the President of China from 1923 to 1924, as well as the military leader of the Zhili clique in the Beiyang Army.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: During the First Sino-Japanese War in _____, he went with the army to fight in Joseon
Cao Kun.fact: During the First Sino-Japanese War in 1894, he went with the army to fight in Joseon.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: After the war was over he joined _____ to participate in the training of the New Army (known as the Beiyang Army)
Cao Kun.fact: After the war was over he joined Yuan Shikai to participate in the training of the New Army (known as the Beiyang Army).

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Admired by _____, Cao managed to rise very quickly
Cao Kun.fact: After the war was over he joined Yuan Shikai to participate in the training of the New Army (known as the Beiyang Army). Admired by Yuan, Cao managed to rise very quickly.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: By the time of the _____ Xinhai Revolution he commanded the Beiyang 3rd Division
Cao Kun.fact: By the time of the 1911 Xinhai Revolution he commanded the Beiyang 3rd Division.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He was a staunch supporter of _____, an opponent of liberalism and communism
Cao Kun.fact: He was a staunch supporter of Confucianism, an opponent of liberalism and communism.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He was made a general in the _____ and led the Zhili clique after the death of Feng Guozhang
Cao Kun.fact: He was made a general in the Beiyang Army and led the Zhili clique after the death of Feng Guozhang.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: During the _____ election he was promised the vice-presidency by Duan Qirui but the office remained vacant after most of the National Assembly left, depriving it of a quorum
Cao Kun.fact: During the 1918 election he was promised the vice-presidency by Duan Qirui but the office remained vacant after most of the National Assembly left, depriving it of a quorum.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He felt betrayed by Duan and defeated him in battle in _____
Cao Kun.fact: He felt betrayed by Duan and defeated him in battle in 1920.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: After forcing the resignations of both Xu Shichang and Li Yuanhong, and engaging in bribery, he became president of China (in Beijing) on 10 October _____, serving to 2 November 1924
Cao Kun.fact: After forcing the resignations of both Xu Shichang and Li Yuanhong, and engaging in bribery, he became president of China (in Beijing) on 10 October 1923, serving to 2 November 1924.

Cao Kun.question: Unfortunately, the airline's 3-day trial tour ended in disaster: the plane crashed on approach to _____, killing all 14 onboard

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Ren.fact: Yuan Shao attempted to cut off Cao Cao's route to the west by sending Han Meng (韓猛) southwest. Cao Ren responded to the threat by defeating Han Meng at Jiluo Hill (雞洛山; located 50 li northeast of present-day Xinmi, Henan).

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: During one battle near _____ (壺關; present-day Huguan County, Shanxi), Cao Cao gave orders that all the enemy troops would be buried alive after the city fell
Cao Ren.fact: During one battle near Hu Pass (壺關; present-day Huguan County, Shanxi), Cao Cao gave orders that all the enemy troops would be buried alive after the city fell.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: However, unlike what everyone thought, _____ managed to create havoc around the Wu's army with just 100 men left by then
Cao Ren.fact: Cao Ren was aware that his army's morale was low, since they were recently defeated at Red Cliffs, so he ordered his subordinate Niu Jin to lead 300 volunteer soldiers into battle, in the hope that they would display bravery and boost his men's morale. Niu Jin and his men were heavily outnumbered and surrounded by the enemy.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: Cao Ren () (_____ – 6 May 223), courtesy name Zixiao, was a military general serving during the late Eastern Han dynasty of China under the warlord Cao Cao, who was also his older second cousin
Cao Ren.fact: Cao Ren () (168 – 6 May 223), courtesy name Zixiao, was a military general serving during the late Eastern Han dynasty of China under the warlord Cao Cao, who was also his older second cousin.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: In the autumn of 219, _____'s general Guan Yu, who was in charge of Liu's territories in southern Jing Province, led an army north to attack Fan
Cao Ren.fact: In the autumn of 219, Liu Bei's general Guan Yu, who was in charge of Liu's territories in southern Jing Province, led an army north to attack Fan.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: Cao Cao sent the general _____ to lead seven armies to resist Guan Yu, but the armies were destroyed in a flood when the Han River overflowed due to heavy rains
Cao Ren.fact: Cao Cao sent the general Yu Jin to lead seven armies to resist Guan Yu, but the armies were destroyed in a flood when the Han River overflowed due to heavy rains. Yu Jin surrendered to Guan Yu while his subordinate Pang De refused and was executed by Guan.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: Yu Jin surrendered to _____ while his subordinate Pang De refused and was executed by Guan
Cao Ren.fact: In the autumn of 219, Liu Bei's general Guan Yu, who was in charge of Liu's territories in southern Jing Province, led an army north to attack Fan. Cao Cao sent the general Yu Jin to lead seven armies to resist Guan Yu, but the armies were destroyed in a flood when the Han River overflowed due to heavy rains.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: By the time reinforcements led by _____ arrived, the water level had subsided slightly
Cao Ren.fact: By the time reinforcements led by Xu Huang arrived, the water level had subsided slightly. While Xu Huang was attacking Guan Yu, Cao Ren seized the opportunity to counterattack and break the siege.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: He also received the title "_____ of Chen" (陳侯) and was given 2,000 more taxable households in his marquisate, making it a total of 3,500 households
Cao Ren.fact: He also received the title "Marquis of Chen" (陳侯) and was given 2,000 more taxable households in his marquisate, making it a total of 3,500 households.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Ren.fact: He was posthumously granted the title "Marquis Zhong" (忠侯), which literally means "loyal marquis".

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Ren.fact: He was best remembered for his bravery and courage, which placed him above Zhang Liao among all of Cao Cao's generals.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Ren.fact: Cao Ren's younger brother Cao Chun was also a general under Cao Cao. Cao Tai was succeeded by his son Cao Chu (曹初).

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: The _____ was Emperor of Cao Wei from 226 to 239.
Cao Rui.fact: Cao Rui () (204 or 205 – 22 January 239), courtesy name Yuanzhong, was the second emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period. Based on conflicting accounts of his age, Pei Songzhi calculated that, in order to be Cao Pi's son, Cao Rui could not have been 36 (by East Asian age reckoning) when he died as recorded, so the recorded age was in error; late-Qing scholars Lu Bi (卢弼) and Mao Guangsheng (冒广生) argued instead that Cao Rui was Yuan Xi's son.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: His parentage is in dispute: his mother, _____, was Yuan Xi's wife, but she later remarried Cao Pi, the first ruler of Wei
Cao Rui.fact: His parentage is in dispute: his mother, Lady Zhen, was Yuan Xi's wife, but she later remarried Cao Pi, the first ruler of Wei.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Rui.fact: He devoted many resources into building palaces and ancestral temples, and his reign saw the stalemate between his empire, Shu Han, and Eastern Wu become more entrenched.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He passed the throne to his adopted son _____ and entrusted him to the regency of Cao Shuang and Sima Yi
Cao Rui.fact: He passed the throne to his adopted son Cao Fang and entrusted him to the regency of Cao Shuang and Sima Yi.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Sima Yi became in control of the Wei government from _____ 249, eventually allowing his grandson Sima Yan to usurp the throne in February 266
Cao Rui.fact: Sima Yi became in control of the Wei government from February 249, eventually allowing his grandson Sima Yan to usurp the throne in February 266.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Rui.fact: His father Cao Pi was Cao Cao's oldest surviving son and the heir apparent. His mother Lady Zhen had been the wife of Yuan Shao's son Yuan Xi, but when she was seized by Cao Cao's army in c.mid-September 204, Cao Pi forced her to marry him, and she gave birth to Cao Rui only eight months after the wedding—leading to theories that Cao Rui was actually biologically Yuan Xi's son and not Cao Pi's.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Lady Zhen was not allowed to accompany him to the new capital _____; in August 221, he forced her to commit suicide
Cao Rui.fact: Lady Zhen was not allowed to accompany him to the new capital Luoyang; in August 221, he forced her to commit suicide.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Sometime during his years as the Prince of _____, he married a daughter of an aristocrat, Lady Yu, as his wife and princess
Cao Rui.fact: Because of what happened to Lady Zhen and Cao Rui's unclear origin, even though Cao Rui was the oldest of Cao Pi's sons, he was not created crown prince early in his father's reign, but was only created the Prince of Pingyuan in March 222. Sometime during his years as the Prince of Pingyuan, he married a daughter of an aristocrat, Lady Yu, as his wife and princess.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He apparently had a cordial relationship with _____, who was created empress (in October 222); as she was sonless, his status as heir apparent was not seriously challenged
Cao Rui.fact: He apparently had a cordial relationship with Lady Guo, who was created empress (in October 222); as she was sonless, his status as heir apparent was not seriously challenged.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Rui.fact: His father had appointed three regents for him—his distant cousin Cao Zhen, the steady administrator Chen Qun, and the shrewd strategist Sima Yi.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Rui.fact: Ultimately, Zhuge's campaigns were futile; after his death in 234, his plan was largely abandoned by his successors Jiang Wan and Fei Yi.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Rui.fact: He adopted two sons to be his own—Cao Fang and Cao Xun, whom he created princes on 23 September 235.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He also ordered that the temples of Cao Cao, _____ and himself were not to be torn down in the future
Cao Rui.fact: In June or July 237, Cao Rui took the unprecedented (and unrepeated in Chinese history) action of setting his own temple name of Liezu, while setting the temple names of Cao Cao and Cao Pi. He also ordered that the temples of Cao Cao, Cao Pi and himself were not to be torn down in the future.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: However, the news leaked, and _____ talked about the feast with him anyway
Cao Rui.fact: By 237, Cao Rui's favorite was no longer Empress Mao, but Consort Guo. Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He created _____ empress on 16 January 239 in preparation of allowing her to become empress dowager after his death
Cao Rui.fact: He created Consort Guo empress on 16 January 239 in preparation of allowing her to become empress dowager after his death.

Cao Rui.fact: Yang Fu noted that he did not do so during the funerals of Cao Pi and Empress Dowager Bian, and advised him not to join in the funeral procession.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: The _____ was Chinese politician (died 190 BCE).
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Shen or Cao Can (died 24 September 190 BCE), courtesy name Jingbo (Chinese: 敬伯), was a Chinese military general and politician.

Cao Shen.fact: He served as a chancellor of the Western Han dynasty.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: The townsfolk rebelled against the magistrate and killed him, allowing _____ and his men to enter
Cao Shen.fact: In 209 BC, after the Dazexiang Uprising broke out, the magistrate of Pei County considered rebelling against the Qin dynasty as well, so he heeded Cao Shen and Xiao He's advice to invite Liu Bang back to support him. Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Shen.fact: They scored victories against Wei Bao's forces, the Zhao army at the Battle of Jingxing, and the combined forces of Qi and Chu at the Battle of Wei River.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: In 202 BC, _____ defeated Xiang Yu at the Battle of Gaixia and unified China under his rule
Cao Shen.fact: During this time, Cao Shen was appointed as acting-Left Chancellor of Liu Bang's Han kingdom, and subsequently promoted to Right Chancellor. After the conquest of the Qi kingdom, Cao Shen left Han Xin and returned to Liu Bang's side to join him in resisting Xiang Yu.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: Cao Zhu was in turn succeeded by his son, _____ (曹奇; died 153 BC), who helped Emperor Jing suppress the Rebellion of the Seven States
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Zhu was in turn succeeded by his son, Cao Qi (曹奇; died 153 BC), who helped Emperor Jing suppress the Rebellion of the Seven States. Cao Qi's son, Cao Shi (曹時; died 131 BC), married Princess Pingyang, one of Emperor Jing's daughters.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: Cao Qi's son, _____ (曹時; died 131 BC), married Princess Pingyang, one of Emperor Jing's daughters
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Qi's son, Cao Shi (曹時; died 131 BC), married Princess Pingyang, one of Emperor Jing's daughters. Cao Shi's son, Cao Xiang (曹襄; died 115 BC), married Princess Wei (a daughter of Emperor Wu and Empress Wei Zifu) and served as a general in the Han campaigns against the Xiongnu.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: The _____ was Chinese general and Cao Wei regent (died 249).
Cao Shuang.fact: Cao Shuang (died 9 February 249), courtesy name Zhaobo, was a Chinese military general and regent of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: He was the eldest son of _____, a prominent general of Cao Wei
Cao Shuang.fact: He was the eldest son of Cao Zhen, a prominent general of Cao Wei.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: He initially held great power in _____ as General-in-Chief but later lost his power to Sima Yi in the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs and was executed on charges of treason
Cao Shuang.fact: Cao Shuang (died 9 February 249), courtesy name Zhaobo, was a Chinese military general and regent of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China. He was the eldest son of Cao Zhen, a prominent general of Cao Wei.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: After ascending the throne in June 226, _____ bestowed upon Shuang several titles of increasing seniority and prestige over his reign
Cao Shuang.fact: When Cao Rui was still his father's heir, he favored Cao Shuang greatly. After ascending the throne in June 226, Cao Rui bestowed upon Shuang several titles of increasing seniority and prestige over his reign.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: Around 239, when the Wei emperor _____ became critically ill, he resolved to pass the throne to his adopted son, Cao Fang
Cao Shuang.fact: When Cao Rui was still his father's heir, he favored Cao Shuang greatly. After ascending the throne in June 226, Cao Rui bestowed upon Shuang several titles of increasing seniority and prestige over his reign.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: However, his trusted officials Liu Fang (劉放) and Sun Zi (孫資), who were unfriendly with Xiahou Xian and _____, became apprehensive upon hearing that Cao Rui wanted to appoint them as regents
Cao Shuang.fact: He initially wanted to entrust Cao Fang to his uncle Cao Yu, to serve as the lead regent, along with Xiahou Xian (夏侯獻), Cao Shuang, Cao Zhao (曹肇; son of Cao Xiu) and Qin Lang. However, his trusted officials Liu Fang (劉放) and Sun Zi (孫資), who were unfriendly with Xiahou Xian and Cao Zhao, became apprehensive upon hearing that Cao Rui wanted to appoint them as regents.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: He was also often at odds with his co-regent _____, who had greater influence and support
Cao Shuang.fact: He was also often at odds with his co-regent Sima Yi, who had greater influence and support. In 243, Sima Yi's position was further strengthened by another successful deployment: Zhuge Ke, a general of Wei's rival state, Eastern Wu, was constantly sending agents to Shouchun (壽春; around present-day Shou County, Anhui) to prepare an invasion, so Sima Yi led Wei forces to Shu County (舒縣), Lujiang Commandery (盧江郡) near the Wei–Wu border.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: Upon hearing the news, the Wu emperor _____ immediately ordered Zhuge Ke to withdraw to Chaisang (柴桑), Yuzhang Commandery (豫章郡)
Cao Shuang.fact: Upon hearing the news, the Wu emperor Sun Quan immediately ordered Zhuge Ke to withdraw to Chaisang (柴桑), Yuzhang Commandery (豫章郡).

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: While it was ostensibly a promotion for _____, the position of Grand Tutor was in fact an honorary one without any real authority over military affairs
Cao Shuang.fact: Sima Yi's popularity and influence instantly multiplied as he was cheered as being able to scare away the enemy numbering over 100,000 without a fight and thus secured the border and saved Shouchun from certain attack. Cao Shuang, feeling insecure over Sima Yi's triumph, managed to persuade the emperor Cao Fang to promote Sima Yi to the position of Grand Tutor (太傅).

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: However, two months later, he lost to Shu forces led by _____ and Fei Yi at the Battle of Xingshi and barely escaped back to Chang'an
Cao Shuang.fact: However, two months later, he lost to Shu forces led by Wang Ping and Fei Yi at the Battle of Xingshi and barely escaped back to Chang'an.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: At the same time, _____'s popularity and influence further increased due to his opposition to the campaign from the start
Cao Shuang.fact: At the same time, Sima Yi's popularity and influence further increased due to his opposition to the campaign from the start. Potentially to deceive Cao Shuang into letting down his guard, Sima Yi stopped engaging in any political activity in May 247 and retired on the grounds of illness.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: According to _____, Sima Yi misheard "Jing Province" as "Bing Province"
Cao Shuang.fact: In the winter of 248, Cao Shuang's protégé, Li Sheng, was appointed as the Inspector of Jing Province by the Wei imperial court. Cao Shuang and his followers overjoyed when Li Sheng reported that Sima Yi was indeed ill and that he could not even hear what Li Sheng said.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: After that, they proceeded to go on a hunting expedition outside _____
Cao Shuang.fact: On 5 February 249, Cao Shuang and his two brothers, Cao Xi (曹羲) and Cao Xun (曹訓), left the imperial capital Luoyang to accompany the emperor Cao Fang to pay respects to his ancestors at the Gaoping Tombs (高平陵). After that, they proceeded to go on a hunting expedition outside Luoyang.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: The _____ was Chinese poet, writer and translator.
Cao Shui.fact: Cao Shui (simplified Chinese: 曹谁; traditional Chinese: 曹誰; pinyin: Cáo Shuí; born June 5, 1982), also called Shawn Cao, courtesy name Yaou (Eurasian), pseudonym or hao Lord of Tower of Babel, is a Chinese poet, novelist, screenwriter and translator.

Cao Shui.fact: He is one of the representative figures of Chinese Contemporary Literature.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: His most notable works include the Epic of _____, Secret of Heaven (trilogy), and King Peacock (TV series)
Cao Shui.fact: His most notable works include the Epic of Eurasia, Secret of Heaven (trilogy), and King Peacock (TV series). His works are dedicated to rebuilding a republic in which the whole humanity can live in freedom, which he always described as Eurasia, the Top of the Tower of Babel or Kunlun Mountains (Heaven Mountains).
